Measles Is Back in the U.S. What Happens Next?

On Nov. 17, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) declared that measles is no longer considered "eliminated" in the U.S. In the past year, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recorded more than 5,800 cases of measles—the highest caseload since 1991.
